zpl_commands.name: ^A Command
zpl_commands.description: The ^A command specifies the font to use in a text field. ^A designates the font for the current ^FD statement or field. The font specified by ^A is used only once for that ^FD entry. If a value for ^A is not specified again, the default ^CF font is used for the next ^FD entry. Scalable/Bitmapped Font

parameters.name: f = font name
parameters.description:
Values: A through Z, and 0 to 9
Any font in the printer (downloaded, EPROM, stored fonts, fonts A through Z and 0
to 9).
IMPORTANT: Parameter f is required. If f is omitted it defaults to the last
value of the ^CF command.

o = field
orientation
parameters.description:
Values:
N = normal
R = rotated 90 degrees (clockwise)
I = inverted 180 degrees
B = read from bottom up, 270 degrees
Default: the last accepted ^FW value or the ^FW default

parameters.name:
h = Character
Height (in dots)
parameters.description:
Scalable
Values: 10 to 32000
Default: last accepted ^CF
Bitmapped
Values: multiples of height from 1 to 10 times the standard height, in increments of
1
Default: last accepted ^CF

parameters.name: w = width (in dots)
parameters.description:
Scalable
Values: 10 to 32000
Default: last accepted ^CF
Bitmapped
Values: multiples of width from 1 to 10 times the standard width, in increments of 1
Default: last accepted ^CF

zpl_commands.name: ^A@ Command
zpl_commands.description: The ^A@ command uses the complete name of a font, rather than the character designation used in ^A. Once a value for ^A@ is defined, it represents that font until a new font name is specified by ^A@. Use Font Name to Call Font

parameters.name: o = field orientation
parameters.description:
Values:
N = normal
R = rotates 90 degrees (clockwise)
I = inverted 180 degrees
B = read from bottom up, 270 degrees
Default: N or the last ^FW value

parameters.name:
h = character height (in
dots)
parameters.description:
Default:
Specifies magnification by w (character width) or the last accepted ^CF
value. Uses the base height if none is specified.
• Scalable - The value is the height in dots of the entire character block.
Magnification factors are unnecessary, because characters are scaled.
• Bitmapped - The value is rounded to the nearest integer multiple of
the font’s base height, then divided by the font’s base height to give a
magnification nearest limit.

parameters.name: w = width (in dots)
parameters.description:
Default: Specifies magnification by h (height) or the last accepted ^CF
value. Specifies the base width is used if none is specified.
• Scalable - The value is the width in dots of the entire character block.
Magnification factors are unnecessary, because characters are scaled.
• Bitmapped - The value rounds to the nearest integer multiple of the
font’s base width, then divided by the font’s base width to give a
magnification nearest limit.

parameters.name: d = drive location of font
parameters.description:
Values: R:, E:, B:, and A:
Default: R:

parameters.name: f = font name
parameters.description:
Values: any valid font
Default: if an invalid or no name is entered, the default set by ^CF is used If
no font has been specified in ^CF, font A is used.
The font named carries over on all subsequent ^A@ commands without a
font name.

x = extension

V50.14.x, or later.
parameters.description:
Values:
.FNT = font
.TTF = TrueType Font
.TTE = TrueType Extension

zpl_commands.name: ^B7 Command
zpl_commands.description: The ^B7 command produces the PDF417 barcode, a two-dimensional, multirow, continuous, stacked symbology. PDF417 is capable of encoding over 1,000 characters per barcode. It is ideally suited for applications requiring large amounts of information at the time the barcode is read. PDF417 Bar Code

dots)

Values: 1 to height of label
Default: value set by ^BY
This number multiplied by the module equals the height of the individual rows

correction and increases the symbol size.

200.

200. The number of rows and columns in the symbol is automatically
determined. You might want to force the number of rows and columns to a
larger value to achieve uniform symbol size. In the current implementation,

zpl_commands.description: The ^GF command allows you to download graphic field data directly into the printer’s bitmap storage area. parameters.description:
Values:
A = ASCII hexadecimal (follows the format for other download commands)
B = binary (data sent after the c parameter is strictly binary)
C = compressed binary (data sent after the c parameter is in compressed
binary format. The data is compressed on the host side using Zebra’s
compression algorithm. The data is then decompressed and placed directly
into the bitmap.)
Default: A

parameters.name: b = binary byte count
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the total number of bytes to be transmitted for the total image or
the total number of bytes that follow parameter d. For ASCII download, the
parameter should match parameter c. Out-of-range values are set to the
nearest limit.
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name:
c = graphic field
count
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the total number of bytes comprising the graphic format (width x
height), which is sent as parameter d. Count divided by bytes per row gives the
number of lines in the image. This number represents the size of the image,
not necessarily the size of the data stream (see d).
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name: d = bytes per row
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the number of bytes in the downloaded data that comprise one row of
the image.
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name: data = data
parameters.description:
Values:
ASCII hexadecimal data: 00 to FF
A string of ASCII hexadecimal numbers, two digits per image byte. CR and LF
can be inserted as needed for readability. The number of two-digit number
pairs must match the above count. Any numbers sent after count is satisfied
are ignored. A comma in the data pads the current line with 00 (white space),
minimizing the data sent. ~DN or any caret or tilde character prematurely
aborts the download.
Binary data: Strictly binary data is sent from the host. All control prefixes are
ignored until the total number of bytes needed for the graphic format is sent.

When PAUSE is pressed, the label reprints (if ^JZ is set to reprint). If a bar
code is near the upper edge of a label, the label feeds out far enough for
the bar code to be verified and then backfeeds to allow the next label to be
printed and verified.
2 = maximum throughput—the printer stops when a verification error is
detected. The printer starts printing the next label while the verifier is still
checking the previous label. This mode provides maximum throughput, but
does not allow the printer to stop immediately on a label with a verification
error.

the label forward.

the label forward.

been printed and positioned.

been printed and positioned.

zpl_commands.name: ~JL Command

zpl_commands.description: The ^JM command lowers the density of the print—24 dots/mm becomes 12, 12 dots/mm becomes 6, 8 dots/mm becomes 4, and 6 dots/mm becomes 3. ^JM also affects the field origin (^FO) placement on the label (see example below). Set Dots per Millimeter

zpl_commands.name: ~JN Command
zpl_commands.description: The ~JN command turns on the head test option. When activated, ~JN causes the printer to halt when a head test failure is encountered. Head Test Fatal Once an error is encountered the printer remains in error mode until the head test is turned off (~JO) or

zpl_commands.name: ~JO Command
zpl_commands.description: The ~JO command configures the printer to run the head test with error reporting enabled. When ~JO is used an error will be displayed and printing will stop if the head test fails. The user can push the PAUSE button on the printer to bypass the error. This command differs from the ~JN (Head Test Fatal) command in that a power cycle is not required in the event of a head test failure.

zpl_commands.name: ~JP Command
zpl_commands.description: The ~JP command clears the format currently being processed and places the printer into Pause Mode.

zpl_commands.name: ~JQ Command
zpl_commands.description: The ~JQ command is used when Zebra BASIC Interpreter is active. Sending ~JQ to the printer terminates the ZBI session. Terminate Zebra BASIC Interpreter Identifies features that are available in printers with firmware version V60.16.2Z, V53.16.2Z, or later.

zpl_commands.name: ~JR Command
zpl_commands.description: The ~JR command resets all of the printer’s internal software, performs a power-on self-test (POST), clears the buffer and DRAM, and resets communication parameters and default values. Issuing a ~JR command performs the same function as a manual power-on reset. Power On Reset

zpl_commands.description: The ^SF command allows you to serialize a standard ^FD string. The maximum size of the mask and increment string is 3K combined. parameters.name: a = mask string

The mask string sets the serialization scheme. The length of the string mask
defines the number of characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) in the current ^FD string to be serialized.
The mask is aligned to the characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) in the ^FD string starting with the right-most
(or in firmware x.14 and later, last) in the backing store position.
Mask String placeholders:D
or d – Decimal numeric 0–9
H or h – Hexadecimal 0–9 plus a-f or A-F
O or o – Octal 0–7
A or a – Alphabetic A–Z or a–z
N or n – Alphanumeric 0–9 plus A–Z or a–z
% – Ignore character or skip

parameters.name: b = increment string
parameters.description:
The increment string is the value to be added to the field on each label.
The default value is equivalent to a decimal value of one. The string
is composed of any characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) defined in the serial string. Invalid characters
(or in firmware version x.14 and later, combining semantic clusters) are
assumed to be equal to a value of zero in that characters (or in firmware
version x.14 and later, combining semantic clusters) position.
The increment value for alphabetic strings starts with ‘A’ or ‘a’ as the
zero placeholder. This means to increment an alphabetic character (or in
firmware version x.14 and later, combining semantic cluster) by one, a value
of ‘B’ or ‘b’ must be in the increment string.

zbi_commands.name: Command and Function Reference Format
zbi_commands.description: This section describes how commands and functions are presented in this document. Function Rules Functions built into this interpreter can be used in expressions only. The function names are not case sensitive.
zbi_commands.format: This section describes how commands and functions are presented in this document.

zbi_commands.name: NEW
zbi_commands.description: This command clears the interpreter’s memory, including the line buffer and variables, but not any open ports. Use this command when creating code to restart the coding process or before resending a program from a file to the interpreter.

zbi_commands.name: REM
zbi_commands.description: A numbered remark line starts with REM and includes text in any form after it. This line is ignored by the interpreter.

zbi_commands.name: ! (EXCLAMATION MARK)
zbi_commands.description: The exclamation mark is the marker for adding comments to the end of numbered programming lines. Any text following the ! is ignored when the line or command is processed.

zbi_commands.name: LIST
zbi_commands.description: This command lists the program lines currently in memory.

zbi_commands.name: AUTONUM
zbi_commands.description: This command automatically generates sequential program line numbers.

zbi_commands.name: RENUM
zbi_commands.description: This command renumbers the lines of the program being edited. RENUM can reorganize code when line numbers become over- or under-spaced. The line references following GOTO and GOSUB statements are renumbered if they are constant numeric values. Renumbering does not occur if the line numbers are outside of the range limits of 1 to 10000.

zbi_commands.name: ECHO
zbi_commands.description: When Console Mode is enabled, this command controls whether the printer echoes the characters back

zbi_commands.name: RUN
zbi_commands.description: This command executes the current program, starting with the lowest line number. The interpreter will continue to execute the program lines in order unless a control statement directs the flow to a different point. When a higher line number does not exist or the END command is processed, the RUN command will stop.

zbi_commands.name: CTRL-C
zbi_commands.description: Sending an end-of-transmission character, ETX (3 in hex), to the console (port 0) terminates the ZBI program currently running.

zbi_commands.name: RESTART
zbi_commands.description: If a program was halted by a break point or the BREAK command, the RESTART command can be used to reactivate the program at the point it stopped. RESTART functions similar to RUN, except the program attempts to restart from the point where it was last terminated. It also works in conjunction with the STEP command, picking up where the STEP command ended.

zbi_commands.name: STEP
zbi_commands.description: If a program was stopped by a BREAK command, STEP attempts to execute the program one line from where it last ended. If the program has not been run or has been completed, this executes the lowest numbered line.

zbi_commands.name: DEBUG
zbi_commands.description: DEBUG enables and disables the TRACE and BREAK commands.

zbi_commands.name: TRACE
zbi_commands.description: This command enables you to debug an application by outputting the executed line numbers and changed variables to the console.

zbi_commands.name: BREAK
zbi_commands.description: This command allows you to stop the program when the program reaches this line.

zbi_commands.name: ADDBREAK
zbi_commands.description: This command allows you to stop the program when the program reaches a specified line.

zbi_commands.name: DELBREAK
zbi_commands.description: This command allows you to remove existing breakpoints.

zbi_commands.name: ZPL
zbi_commands.description: This command terminates and exits the ZBI environment.

zbi_commands.name: LET
zbi_commands.description: The LET command is used to assign value to a specific variable. The expression is evaluated and assigned to each variable in the variable list.

zbi_commands.name: IF Statements
zbi_commands.description: Executes or skips a sequence of statements, depending on the value of a Boolean expression. DO Loops Repeats instructions based on the results of a comparison. FOR Loops A control flow statement which allows code to be executed iteratively.

zbi_commands.name: DO Loops
zbi_commands.description: Processing of the loop is controlled by a <WHILE/UNTIL> expression located on the DO or LOOP line. Processing a WHILE statement is the same on either the DO or LOOP lines. The Boolean expression is evaluated and if the statement is true, the LOOP continues at the line after the DO statement. Otherwise, the line after the corresponding LOOP is the next line to be processed. Processing an UNTIL statement is the same on either the DO or LOOP lines. The Boolean expression is

zbi_commands.name: FOR Loops
zbi_commands.description: FOR loops are an easy way to iterate through a range of values and run a body of code for each value iterated.

zbi_commands.name: GOTO/GOSUB
zbi_commands.description: GOSUB is followed by a line number. The program will attempt to process the line the GOSUB command points to rather than the next line of the program. Upon executing the GOSUB statement, the interpreter continues running at the line number specified following GOSUB. If the line number referenced does not exist, an error will occur. Before executing the next line, the GOSUB command stores the line number of the GOSUB line. When the

zbi_commands.name: SUB
zbi_commands.description: This command allows you to use names instead of actual line numbers as the target of GOSUBs and GOTOs. AUTONUM can be used at the beginning of a file and there is no need to compute the line number where the jump will go.

zbi_commands.name: EXIT
zbi_commands.description: This command is used to exit the DO and FOR loops.

zbi_commands.name: END
zbi_commands.description: The END command terminates any program currently running. When the END command is received, the

zbi_commands.name: OPEN
zbi_commands.description: This command is used to open a port for transmitting and receiving data.

zbi_commands.name: CLOSE
zbi_commands.description: This command is implemented to close specific ports that are in use. If a port is open on a channel and the

zbi_commands.name: DATAREADY
zbi_commands.description: This function is used to determine if there is data received on a specified port.
zbi_commands.returns: 1 if there is data, 0 if there is no data.

zbi_commands.name: SERVERSOCKET
zbi_commands.description: This function opens a listening socket for incoming UDP packets or TCP connections. It must be used in conjunction with the ACCEPT function.
zbi_commands.returns: NUMERIC = returns the handle of the server upon success.

zbi_commands.name: SERVERCLOSE
zbi_commands.description: This function closes a listening server socket created by SERVERSOCKET.
zbi_commands.returns: Returns a 0 if the socket was already closed or a 1 if the socket was closed successfully.

zbi_commands.name: CLIENTSOCKET
zbi_commands.description: This function creates an outgoing TCP connection or sets up UDP transmissions. Once set up for UDP, packets can be sent by printing to the socket. Packets are sent when the size limit is met or a EOT character is written.
zbi_commands.returns: The port number assigned to the connection.

zbi_commands.name: ACCEPT
zbi_commands.description: This function will accept incoming TCP or UDP connections and assign a channel for the connection. SERVERSOCKET must be used to set up the listening socket before ACCEPT can be used.
zbi_commands.returns: The channel number to use to communicate with the client.

sgd_commands.description: power.wake.radio This command is used to enable or disable the power wake feature on printers that are radio (WLAN, BT Classic, and BTLE) enabled. The radio must be enabled to support waking on that interface. i.e.
possible_values: "on" ZQ3 with BT Classic/BTLE radio installed (BT Only - UART)
"off" ZQ5 with WLAN/BT Classic radio installed
"on" ZQ5 with BT Classic/BTLE radio installed (BT Only - UART)
"on" "off" ZD4xx, ZD6xx with WLAN/BT Classic/BTLE installed
"off" ZD4xx, ZD6xx with BTLE only radio or no radio installed

sgd_commands.name: power.current
sgd_commands.description: power.current This command returns the battery pack instantaneous current value in mA for printers supporting Power Precision Plus batteries.

sgd_commands.name: power.temperature
sgd_commands.description: power.temperature Returns the current battery temperature in degrees Celsius for printers that support a Power Precision Plus and Smart Batteries.

sgd_commands.name: power.percent_health
sgd_commands.description: power.percent_health This command returns the percent health that is read from the fuel gauge for printers that support a Power Precision Plus battery. The battery health is expressed as a percentage of design capacity.

sgd_commands.name: power.part_number
sgd_commands.description: power.part_number Returns the battery part number for printers that support Power Precision Plus batteries.

sgd_commands.name: power.sleep.cradle
sgd_commands.description: power.sleep.cradle This command enables or disables the sleep timeout feature while the printer is docked in the cradle. In the ZQ5 printer, the sleep timeout in the cradle is enabled by default. In the ZQ3 and ZQ6 printers, the
possible_values: "enabled" indicates that power.sleep.timeout is honored while the printer is docked in a
"disabled" indicates that power.sleep.timeout is disabled while the printer is docked in

sgd_commands.name: power.remaining_capacity
sgd_commands.description: power.remaining_capacity This command returns the remaining capacity of the battery in milliamp hours (mAh).

sgd_commands.name: power.cycle_count
sgd_commands.description: power.cycle_count This command returns the number of charge cycles the battery has performed. A cycle is defined as a discharge of 80% of the pack's full charge capacity plus the concatenated partial charges that add to 80%

sgd_commands.name: print.legacy_compatibility
sgd_commands.description: print.legacy_compatibility This command turns off or on the legacy compatibility print quality.
possible_values: "on" uses legacy QLn print quality tables. Applicable to ZQ610 and ZQ620 printers only. Not

sgd_commands.name: print.tone
sgd_commands.description: print.tone This command specifies the printer darkness.
possible_values: "-0.1" to "-30.0" and "+0.1" to "+30.0" for incremental adjustments

sgd_commands.name: print.troubleshooting_label_print
sgd_commands.description: print.troubleshooting_label_print Sets whether batch counters will be displayed on the printer’s control panel.
possible_values: "enabled" specifies that batch counters will be displayed
"disabled" specifies that batch counters will not be displayed

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.serial_number
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.serial_number Sets the ribbon’s part number.
possible_values: An alpha-numeric string between 0 and 64 characters.

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.part_number
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.part_number Sets the ribbon’s part number.
possible_values: An alpha-numeric string between 0 and 64 characters.

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.part_number
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.part_number This command retrieves the part number of the ribbon cartridge installed in the printer. There is a 12 character max for the size of string returned since the cartridge allows for 10 character part numbers.

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.length_remaining
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.length_remaining This command retrieves the length of ribbon remaining on the cartridge. This is specified in meters. If a cartridge is not installed, the printer returns "0". If the cartridge option is not available in the printer,

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.length
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.length This command returns the original length of the ribbon cartridge installed in the printer. This is specified in meters. If a ribbon cartridge is not installed, then the printer returns "0". If the ribbon cartridge option is not

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.authenticated
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.authenticated This command returns the printer cartridge authentication status. The setting gets updated every time an authentication occurs (power up, head close, or any other time).

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.inserted
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.inserted This command returns if the ribbon cartridge is inserted or not. The command is hidden in an ALLCV.

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.coating
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.coating This command sets the type of ribbon coating used.
possible_values: To configure the printer for the printer ribbon:

sgd_commands.name: ribbon.tension
sgd_commands.description: ribbon.tension This command sets the tension of the ribbon.

sgd_commands.name: rtc.exists
sgd_commands.description: rtc.exists This command reports whether the system has a real-time clock.
possible_values: "no" the system does not have a real-time clock.
"yes" the system has a real-time clock.

sgd_commands.name: rtc.date
sgd_commands.description: rtc.date The command sets the system date. The command accepts the month-day-year format, for example, "11-02-2021". If the format is not correct or the date is not valid, the command is ignored. The printer needs

sgd_commands.name: rtc.time
sgd_commands.description: rtc.time This command sets the system time. The time value must be in the hour:minute:second format, for example, 11:32:11. If the format is not correct or the time is not valid, the command is ignored. The printer

sgd_commands.name: rtc.timezone
sgd_commands.description: rtc.timezone This command specifies the POSIX-compliant time zone string. This string includes the following:
possible_values: www.iana.org/time-zones This site is updated periodically to reflect changes made by political
bodies to time zone boundaries, UTC offsets, and daylight-saving rules.

sgd_commands.name: rtc.unix_timestamp
sgd_commands.description: rtc.unix_timestamp This command sets or gets the printer time based on the Unix Epoch (UTC) number of seconds since January 1, 1970.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.air_pressure.current_reading
sgd_commands.description: sensor.air_pressure.current_reading This command returns the atmospheric pressure in millibars.
possible_values: "" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.ambient_light.current_reading
sgd_commands.description: sensor.ambient_light.current_reading This command returns the ambient light value. The ambient light reading is reported in lux.
possible_values: "" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.battery.in_volts
sgd_commands.description: sensor.battery.in_volts This command retrieves information on the battery current in volts.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.brightness
sgd_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.brightness This command retrieves the current back bar sensor brightness level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.ppr_out_thold
sgd_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.ppr_out_thold This command retrieves the current back bar sensor paper out threshold value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.cur
sgd_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.cur This command retrieves the current back bar sensor value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.cover_open
sgd_commands.description: sensor.cover_open This printer setting determines if the printer media cover is open.
possible_values: "yes" means the printer cover is open
"no" means the printer cover is closed

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.ppr_out_thold
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.ppr_out_thold This command retrieves the current paper out threshold level of the front bar sensor of the printer.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.cur
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.cur This command retrieves the current front bar sensor value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.thold
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.thold This command retrieves the current front bar sensor threshold value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.gain
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.gain This command retrieves the current front bar sensor gain level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.brightness
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.brightness This command retrieves the current front bar sensor brightness.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.offset
sgd_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.offset This command retrieves the current front bar sensor offset value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.offset
sgd_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.offset This command retrieves the current back bar sensor offset value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.gap.thold
sgd_commands.description: sensor.gap.thold This command retrieves the current gap sensor threshold level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.gap.offset
sgd_commands.description: sensor.gap.offset This command retrieves the current gap sensor offset value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.gap.gain
sgd_commands.description: sensor.gap.gain This command retrieves the current gap sensor gain level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.gap.brightness
sgd_commands.description: sensor.gap.brightness This command retrieves the current gap sensor brightness level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.head.temp_avg
sgd_commands.description: sensor.head.temp_avg This command retrieves the current average head temperature in Celsius.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.head.temp_celsius
sgd_commands.description: sensor.head.temp_celsius This command retrieves the current head temperature in Celsius.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.head.temp
sgd_commands.description: sensor.head.temp This command retrieves the current head temperature of the printer.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.magnetometer.current_reading
sgd_commands.description: sensor.magnetometer.current_reading This command returns a magnetic induction reading in gauss.
possible_values: The magnetic induction in gauss. If the sensor is not installed, the getvar returns "".

sgd_commands.name: sensor.object_temperature.current_reading
sgd_commands.description: sensor.object_temperature.current_reading This command returns the temperature, in Celsius, from the sensor.
possible_values: Object temperature, in degrees Celsius, from "-20.0" to "200.0".
"" indicates that the temperature sensor is not installed.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.peel.thold
sgd_commands.description: sensor.peel.thold This command retrieves the current peel sensor threshold level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.peel.gain
sgd_commands.description: sensor.peel.gain This command retrieves the current peel sensor gain level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.paper_supply
sgd_commands.description: sensor.paper_supply Returns current paper supply status.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.peeler
sgd_commands.description: sensor.peeler Obtains current peeler sensor status.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.peel.brightness
sgd_commands.description: sensor.peel.brightness This command returns the current peel sensor brightness level.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.proximity.current_reading
sgd_commands.description: sensor.proximity.current_reading This command returns proximity information. The higher the number, the closer the item is.
possible_values: "0" to "4095" A higher number indicates closer proximity.
"" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.width.in_dots
sgd_commands.description: sensor.width.in_dots This command retrieves the current width sensor value in dots.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.width.cur
sgd_commands.description: sensor.width.cur This command retrieves the current width sensor value.

sgd_commands.name: sensor.self_adjusting_enable
sgd_commands.description: sensor.self_adjusting_enable Enables the self-adjusting gap sensor.
possible_values: "yes" enables the self-adjusting gap sensor and disables the traditional gap sensor
"no" disables the self-adjusting gap sensor and enables the traditional gap sensor

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.device_id_string
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.device_id_string This command retrieves the manufacturer assigned IEEE1284 Device Identification string for USB devices.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.device_unique_id
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.device_unique_id This command sets the USB Unique Device ID setting. The identifier that makes any printer unique is set by the "usb.device.serial_string" command which is reported to the USB driver.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.device_version
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.device_version This command returns the version of the USB device being queried.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.manufacturer_string
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.manufacturer_string This command retrieves the USB device manufacturer’s name.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.product_id
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.product_id This command retrieves the Product Identification number that a manufacturer assigned to a particular product. This number, along with the Vendor ID, allows a USB host to distinguish between devices.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.product_string
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.product_string This command returns the manufacturer-assigned string describing a particular USB product.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.serial_string
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.serial_string This command returns the manufacturer-assigned serial number for a particular USB product.

sgd_commands.name: usb.device.vendor_id
sgd_commands.description: usb.device.vendor_id This command returns the Vendor Identification number that the USB-IF organization has assigned to a manufacturer. This number, along with the Product ID, allows a USB host to distinguish between devices.

sgd_commands.name: usb.halt
sgd_commands.description: usb.halt This command controls whether the printer allows communication over the USB port when the printer is in an error condition.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.config_info_to_usb
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.config_info_to_usb This command is used by WML to save the ^HH output files to the USB thumb drive. The file names are written in the CONFIGxxx.TXT format, where xxx ranges from 1 to 999.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.fn_field_data
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.fn_field_data This command is used to collect a user’s response to a presented ^FN prompt. IMPORTANT: This command is used only in the context of the on-printer Print Station application.
possible_values: The text entered by the user via a USB Human Interface Device (HID) keyboard.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.fn_last_field
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.fn_last_field This command is intended for use by WML code to control the presentation of ^FN fields contained within a template file that resides on the E:/ drive and has an extension of .ZPL.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.hid_count
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.hid_count This command displays the number of USB Human Interface Devices (HIDs) connected to the printer. Refer to http://www.usb.org for further details on USB device types.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.keyboard_input
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.keyboard_input This command enables/disables USB keyboard input to the printer, affecting the Print Station user menu item.
possible_values: "off" means keyboard input is not supported

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.lock_out
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.lock_out This command enables/disables the USB host port.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.mass_storage_count
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.mass_storage_count This command displays the number of USB mass storage devices connected to the printer. Only the first USB mass storage device found will be mounted and accessible.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.read_list
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.read_list This command scans the mounted usb mass storage device for non-user-restricted files and displays the files in a list.
possible_values: "fill_store" The printer creates a list of all of the top-level files that are readable on a
connected mass storage device. (.ZPL and .XML files)
"store" The printer copies the current file (the file listed on the display) or all eligible files if
SELECT ALL is displayed from the USB mass storage device to the printer’s E: drive.
NOTE: "store" does an exact byte-for-byte copy of the file being stored. ZPL files
that are transferred to the printer using the “store” command are NOT prepared to
be used with a recall format command (^XF). See XREF Character Substitution (in
Mirror) for the modifications necessary to prepare a ZPL file for use with ^XF. If the
ZPL file contains a ^DF, the appropriate way to place it on the printer’s memory is to

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.read_list_print_delay
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.read_list_print_delay This command specifies a number of milliseconds for the printer to wait before processing the next file when “SELECT ALL” is chosen on the USB PRINT FILES user menu.

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.template_list
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.template_list This command is used by WML to support selecting .ZPL template files resident on the E:/ drive.
possible_values: "fill" The printer analyzes the contents of its E:/ drive and creates a list of the template files
"up" moves to the previous file in the list
"down" moves to the next file in the list

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.template_print_amount
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.template_print_amount This command is used by WML to control the number of template-type labels to print.
possible_values: "up" moves to the previous file in the list
"down" moves to the next file in the list
sgd_commands.default: "1" which will change based on the contents of the selected template file

sgd_commands.name: usb.host.write_list
sgd_commands.description: usb.host.write_list This command scans the E: flash drive for non-user-restricted files and displays the files in a list.
possible_values: "fill_store" The printer analyzes the contents of its E: drive and creates a list of files that
may be copied to a USB mass storage device connected to the printer.
"store" The printer copies the current file (the file listed on the display) or all eligible files if
"SELECT ALL" is displayed to the USB mass storage device.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.appl_path
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.appl_path This command specifies the path to the location on a USB device from which Mirror files are retrieved. If no path is specified, then the path is zebra/appl.
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.auto
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.auto This command determines if mirroring happens automatically when a USB device is inserted in the printer. To use this function, the setting for usb.mirror.enable must be "on".
possible_values: "on" Mirroring occurs automatically when the USB device is inserted and
"off" Mirroring does not occur automatically when the USB device is inserted.
"prompt" The printer gives you the option to start or abort a mirroring process.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.enable
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.enable This command enables or disables the ability to perform mirroring of a USB device.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.enabled
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.enabled Enables or disables the ability to perform mirroring using a USB device memory stick.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.error_retry
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.error_retry This command specifies the number of times that the USB mirror operation will be repeated if the process fails.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.auto
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.auto This command determines if a feedback file is written to the USB device connected to the printer after mirroring.
possible_values: "on" A feedback file is written to the USB device connected to the printer.
"off" A feeback file is not written to the USB device connected to the printer.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.odometer
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.odometer This command instructs the printer to set or retrieve the usb.mirror.feedback.odometer value.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.path
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.path This command specifies where the feedback file is stored on the USB drive connected to the printer.
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters
NOTE: The path must exist on the USB drive before the printer can write files to it.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.fetch
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.fetch This command immediately initiates a USB mirroring operation. To use this function, the setting for usb.mirror.enable must be "on".

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.last_error
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.last_error This command returns the last USB mirroring error string. If there are no errors, the result is "No Error".

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.last_time
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.last_time This command returns the date and time of the last USB mirroring operation. The date and time reported are from the printer’s clock.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.path
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.path This command specifies the root directory on the connected USB drive. The root directory contains the subdirectories from which files are retrieved during the mirror operation. If no path is specified, then the
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.reset_delay
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.reset_delay This command specifies a number of seconds for the printer to wait after it loads the last of the files in the /commands directory during mirroring.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.success
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.success This command returns the last USB mirroring event status string.
possible_values: "yes" Indicates that the mirroring operation was successful.
"no" Indicates that the mirroring operation was not successful.

sgd_commands.name: usb.mirror.success_time
sgd_commands.description: usb.mirror.success_time This command returns the date and time of the last successful USB mirroring operation. The date and time reported are from the printer’s clock.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.add_breakpoint
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.add_breakpoint This command instructs the printer to set a ZBI program break point.
possible_values: Any line number of the program currently being debugged.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.break
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.break This command breaks the execution of the ZBI 2.0 program that is currently running.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.clear_breakpoints
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.clear_breakpoints This command deletes all breakpoints in the current ZBI 2.0 program.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.delete_breakpoint
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.delete_breakpoint This command deletes a breakpoint in the current ZBI 2.0 program.
possible_values: You can use the same value as add_breakpoint.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.line_number
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.line_number This command gives you control and information about which line of a stopped ZBI 2.0 program is being executed.
possible_values: Any line number of the currently stopped ZBI program.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.restart
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.restart This command restarts a ZBI 2.0 program that is currently stopped.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.run
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.run This command runs the current ZBI 2.0 program that is loaded in the interpreter.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.step
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.step This command restarts the execution of the currently stopped ZBI 2.0 program for one line.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.terminate
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.terminate This command instructs the ZBI 2.0 program to terminate and shuts down the interpreter.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.variable_name
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.variable_name This command sets the name of the variable that is to be read or modified through variable_value.
possible_values: Any ZBI variable in the program that is currently being debugged.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.control.variable_value
sgd_commands.description: zbi.control.variable_value This command identifies the variable name.
possible_values: A string or integer that is dependent on the variable type in variable_name.
sgd_commands.default: The current value of the variable referenced by variable_name.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.enable
sgd_commands.description: zbi.enable This command enables ZBI on the printer.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.key
sgd_commands.description: zbi.key This command identifies if the ZBI 2.0 option is enabled or disabled on the printer.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.last_error
sgd_commands.description: zbi.last_error This command identifies the last error that the ZBI 2.0 interpreter encountered.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.program_list
sgd_commands.description: zbi.program_list This SGD is intended to be used on WML pages. It purpose is to support displaying the name of each ZBI program file contained on the E: drive.
possible_values: "up" gets the previous file in the list
"down" gets the next file in the list
"execute" executes the currently specified zbi file (as determined by the getvar command)

sgd_commands.name: zbi.reseller_key
sgd_commands.description: zbi.reseller_key This command allows programs that are encrypted with this key in ZBI- Developer to run.
possible_values: Any valid encryption key provided by ZBI Developer.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.revision
sgd_commands.description: zbi.revision This command identifies the current ZBI version.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.running_program_name
sgd_commands.description: zbi.running_program_name This command identifies the name of the ZBI 2.0 program that is currently running.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.start_info.execute
sgd_commands.description: zbi.start_info.execute This command instructs the ZBI 2.0 environment to execute the program listed in the file_name.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.start_info.file_name
sgd_commands.description: zbi.start_info.file_name This command prepares a program to run when the zbi.start_info.execute command is used. This command does not run the program.
possible_values: A file name or path of a basic program
sgd_commands.default: The last program run. If nothing has been run, "*:\.BAZ".

sgd_commands.name: zbi.start_info.memory_alloc
sgd_commands.description: zbi.start_info.memory_alloc This command identifies the amount of memory currently in use in a ZBI 2.0 program.

sgd_commands.name: zbi.state
sgd_commands.description: zbi.state This command shows the current state of the ZBI 2.0 program.
possible_values: "running" ZBI Interpreter is active and running a program
"stopped" ZBI Interpreter is active but not executing a program

sgd_commands.name: zpl.calibrate
sgd_commands.description: zpl.calibrate This command measures the media label length that is installed in the printer. It then sets the "zpl.label_length" parameter to the detected media label length.

sgd_commands.name: zpl.format_prefix
sgd_commands.description: zpl.format_prefix This command sets or returns the format character to the character corresponding to the ASCII Hex value xx. This command is similar to the ^CC and ~CC commands.
possible_values: Specifying the up or down will increment or decrement the current value.
Note that the increment/decrement will skip over conflicting values.
Conflicting values for zpl.format_prefix are zpl.command_prefix, and

sgd_commands.name: zpl.caret
sgd_commands.description: zpl.caret This command is used to change the format command prefix for ZPL commands. The default prefix is the caret (^)

sgd_commands.name: zpl.control_character
sgd_commands.description: zpl.control_character This command is used to change the control command prefix. The default prefix is the tilde (~). This command is equivalent to the ^CT and ~CT commands.
possible_values: ASCII values for the desired character "00-FF,00-ff,up,down"
See ASCII on page 1555 for more information.

sgd_commands.name: zpl.delimiter
sgd_commands.description: zpl.delimiter This command is used to change the delimiter character for ZPL commands. The default delimiter character is the comma (,).
possible_values: HEX values for the desired character "00-FF,00-ff,up,down"
See ASCII on page 1555 for more information.

sgd_commands.name: zpl.label_length
sgd_commands.description: zpl.label_length This command defines the length of the label. This command is necessary when using continuous media (media that is not divided into separate labels by gaps, spaces, notches, slots, or holes).
possible_values: "1" to "32000", (in dots) not to exceed the maximum label length.
While the printer accepts any value for this parameter, the amount of memory installed determines
the maximum length of the label.

sgd_commands.name: zpl.label_length_always

sgd_commands.name: ip.mirror.error_retry
sgd_commands.description: ip.mirror.error_retry This command identifies how many times mirroring is retried when an error occurs.

sgd_commands.description: ip.mirror.feedback.freq This command specifies the time interval (in minutes) between performing feedback file uploads.

all_commands.name: ^A@ Command
all_commands.description: The ^A@ command uses the complete name of a font, rather than the character designation used in ^A. Once a value for ^A@ is defined, it represents that font until a new font name is specified by ^A@. Use Font Name to Call Font

parameters.name: o = field orientation
parameters.description:
Values:

R = rotates 90 degrees (clockwise)
I = inverted 180 degrees
B = read from bottom up, 270 degrees
Default: N or the last ^FW value

parameters.name:
h = character height (in
dots)
parameters.description:
Default:
Specifies magnification by w (character width) or the last accepted ^CF
value. Uses the base height if none is specified.
• Scalable - The value is the height in dots of the entire character block.
Magnification factors are unnecessary, because characters are scaled.
• Bitmapped - The value is rounded to the nearest integer multiple of
the font’s base height, then divided by the font’s base height to give a
magnification nearest limit.

parameters.name: w = width (in dots)
parameters.description:
Default: Specifies magnification by h (height) or the last accepted ^CF
value. Specifies the base width is used if none is specified.
• Scalable - The value is the width in dots of the entire character block.
Magnification factors are unnecessary, because characters are scaled.
• Bitmapped - The value rounds to the nearest integer multiple of the
font’s base width, then divided by the font’s base width to give a
magnification nearest limit.

B = binary (data sent after the c parameter is strictly binary)
C = compressed binary (data sent after the c parameter is in compressed
binary format. The data is compressed on the host side using Zebra’s
compression algorithm. The data is then decompressed and placed directly
into the bitmap.)
Default: A

parameters.name: b = binary byte count
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the total number of bytes to be transmitted for the total image or
the total number of bytes that follow parameter d. For ASCII download, the
parameter should match parameter c. Out-of-range values are set to the
nearest limit.
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name:
c = graphic field
count
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the total number of bytes comprising the graphic format (width x
height), which is sent as parameter d. Count divided by bytes per row gives the
number of lines in the image. This number represents the size of the image,
not necessarily the size of the data stream (see d).
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name: d = bytes per row
parameters.description:
Values: 1 to 99999
This is the number of bytes in the downloaded data that comprise one row of
the image.
Default: command is ignored if a value is not specified

parameters.name: data = data
parameters.description:
Values:
ASCII hexadecimal data: 00 to FF
A string of ASCII hexadecimal numbers, two digits per image byte. CR and LF
can be inserted as needed for readability. The number of two-digit number
pairs must match the above count. Any numbers sent after count is satisfied
are ignored. A comma in the data pads the current line with 00 (white space),
minimizing the data sent. ~DN or any caret or tilde character prematurely
aborts the download.
Binary data: Strictly binary data is sent from the host. All control prefixes are
ignored until the total number of bytes needed for the graphic format is sent.

all_commands.name: ^JJ Command
all_commands.description: The ^JJ command allows you to control an online verifier or applicator device. Set Auxiliary Port

When PAUSE is pressed, the label reprints (if ^JZ is set to reprint). If a bar
code is near the upper edge of a label, the label feeds out far enough for
the bar code to be verified and then backfeeds to allow the next label to be
printed and verified.
2 = maximum throughput—the printer stops when a verification error is
detected. The printer starts printing the next label while the verifier is still
checking the previous label. This mode provides maximum throughput, but
does not allow the printer to stop immediately on a label with a verification
error.

the label forward.

been printed and positioned.

been printed and positioned.

all_commands.name: ~JN Command
all_commands.description: The ~JN command turns on the head test option. When activated, ~JN causes the printer to halt when a head test failure is encountered. Head Test Fatal Once an error is encountered the printer remains in error mode until the head test is turned off (~JO) or

all_commands.name: ~JP Command

all_commands.name: ~JQ Command

all_commands.name: ~JR Command

all_commands.description: The ^SF command allows you to serialize a standard ^FD string. The maximum size of the mask and increment string is 3K combined. parameters.name: a = mask string

The mask string sets the serialization scheme. The length of the string mask
defines the number of characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) in the current ^FD string to be serialized.
The mask is aligned to the characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) in the ^FD string starting with the right-most
(or in firmware x.14 and later, last) in the backing store position.
Mask String placeholders:D
or d – Decimal numeric 0–9
H or h – Hexadecimal 0–9 plus a-f or A-F
O or o – Octal 0–7
A or a – Alphabetic A–Z or a–z
N or n – Alphanumeric 0–9 plus A–Z or a–z
% – Ignore character or skip

parameters.name: b = increment string
parameters.description:
The increment string is the value to be added to the field on each label.
The default value is equivalent to a decimal value of one. The string
is composed of any characters (or in firmware version x.14 and later,
combining semantic clusters) defined in the serial string. Invalid characters
(or in firmware version x.14 and later, combining semantic clusters) are
assumed to be equal to a value of zero in that characters (or in firmware
version x.14 and later, combining semantic clusters) position.
The increment value for alphabetic strings starts with ‘A’ or ‘a’ as the
zero placeholder. This means to increment an alphabetic character (or in
firmware version x.14 and later, combining semantic cluster) by one, a value
of ‘B’ or ‘b’ must be in the increment string.

all_commands.name: Command and Function Reference Format
all_commands.description: This section describes how commands and functions are presented in this document. Function Rules Functions built into this interpreter can be used in expressions only. The function names are not case sensitive.
all_commands.format: This section describes how commands and functions are presented in this document.

all_commands.name: NEW
all_commands.description: This command clears the interpreter’s memory, including the line buffer and variables, but not any open ports. Use this command when creating code to restart the coding process or before resending a program from a file to the interpreter.

all_commands.name: REM
all_commands.description: A numbered remark line starts with REM and includes text in any form after it. This line is ignored by the interpreter.

all_commands.name: ! (EXCLAMATION MARK)
all_commands.description: The exclamation mark is the marker for adding comments to the end of numbered programming lines. Any text following the ! is ignored when the line or command is processed.

all_commands.name: LIST
all_commands.description: This command lists the program lines currently in memory.

all_commands.name: AUTONUM
all_commands.description: This command automatically generates sequential program line numbers.

all_commands.name: RENUM
all_commands.description: This command renumbers the lines of the program being edited. RENUM can reorganize code when line numbers become over- or under-spaced. The line references following GOTO and GOSUB statements are renumbered if they are constant numeric values. Renumbering does not occur if the line numbers are outside of the range limits of 1 to 10000.

all_commands.name: ECHO
all_commands.description: When Console Mode is enabled, this command controls whether the printer echoes the characters back

all_commands.name: RUN
all_commands.description: This command executes the current program, starting with the lowest line number. The interpreter will continue to execute the program lines in order unless a control statement directs the flow to a different point. When a higher line number does not exist or the END command is processed, the RUN command will stop.

all_commands.name: CTRL-C
all_commands.description: Sending an end-of-transmission character, ETX (3 in hex), to the console (port 0) terminates the ZBI program currently running.

all_commands.name: RESTART
all_commands.description: If a program was halted by a break point or the BREAK command, the RESTART command can be used to reactivate the program at the point it stopped. RESTART functions similar to RUN, except the program attempts to restart from the point where it was last terminated. It also works in conjunction with the STEP command, picking up where the STEP command ended.

all_commands.name: STEP
all_commands.description: If a program was stopped by a BREAK command, STEP attempts to execute the program one line from where it last ended. If the program has not been run or has been completed, this executes the lowest numbered line.

all_commands.name: DEBUG
all_commands.description: DEBUG enables and disables the TRACE and BREAK commands.

all_commands.name: TRACE
all_commands.description: This command enables you to debug an application by outputting the executed line numbers and changed variables to the console.

all_commands.name: BREAK
all_commands.description: This command allows you to stop the program when the program reaches this line.

all_commands.name: ADDBREAK
all_commands.description: This command allows you to stop the program when the program reaches a specified line.

all_commands.name: DELBREAK
all_commands.description: This command allows you to remove existing breakpoints.

all_commands.name: ZPL
all_commands.description: This command terminates and exits the ZBI environment.

all_commands.name: LET
all_commands.description: The LET command is used to assign value to a specific variable. The expression is evaluated and assigned to each variable in the variable list.

all_commands.name: IF Statements
all_commands.description: Executes or skips a sequence of statements, depending on the value of a Boolean expression. DO Loops Repeats instructions based on the results of a comparison. FOR Loops A control flow statement which allows code to be executed iteratively.

all_commands.name: DO Loops
all_commands.description: Processing of the loop is controlled by a <WHILE/UNTIL> expression located on the DO or LOOP line. Processing a WHILE statement is the same on either the DO or LOOP lines. The Boolean expression is evaluated and if the statement is true, the LOOP continues at the line after the DO statement. Otherwise, the line after the corresponding LOOP is the next line to be processed. Processing an UNTIL statement is the same on either the DO or LOOP lines. The Boolean expression is

all_commands.name: FOR Loops
all_commands.description: FOR loops are an easy way to iterate through a range of values and run a body of code for each value iterated.

all_commands.name: GOTO/GOSUB
all_commands.description: GOSUB is followed by a line number. The program will attempt to process the line the GOSUB command points to rather than the next line of the program. Upon executing the GOSUB statement, the interpreter continues running at the line number specified following GOSUB. If the line number referenced does not exist, an error will occur. Before executing the next line, the GOSUB command stores the line number of the GOSUB line. When the

all_commands.name: SUB
all_commands.description: This command allows you to use names instead of actual line numbers as the target of GOSUBs and GOTOs. AUTONUM can be used at the beginning of a file and there is no need to compute the line number where the jump will go.

all_commands.name: EXIT
all_commands.description: This command is used to exit the DO and FOR loops.

all_commands.name: END
all_commands.description: The END command terminates any program currently running. When the END command is received, the

all_commands.name: OPEN
all_commands.description: This command is used to open a port for transmitting and receiving data.

all_commands.name: CLOSE
all_commands.description: This command is implemented to close specific ports that are in use. If a port is open on a channel and the

all_commands.name: DATAREADY
all_commands.description: This function is used to determine if there is data received on a specified port.
all_commands.returns: 1 if there is data, 0 if there is no data.

all_commands.name: SERVERSOCKET
all_commands.description: This function opens a listening socket for incoming UDP packets or TCP connections. It must be used in conjunction with the ACCEPT function.
all_commands.returns: NUMERIC = returns the handle of the server upon success.

all_commands.name: SERVERCLOSE
all_commands.description: This function closes a listening server socket created by SERVERSOCKET.
all_commands.returns: Returns a 0 if the socket was already closed or a 1 if the socket was closed successfully.

all_commands.name: CLIENTSOCKET
all_commands.description: This function creates an outgoing TCP connection or sets up UDP transmissions. Once set up for UDP, packets can be sent by printing to the socket. Packets are sent when the size limit is met or a EOT character is written.
all_commands.returns: The port number assigned to the connection.

all_commands.name: ACCEPT
all_commands.description: This function will accept incoming TCP or UDP connections and assign a channel for the connection. SERVERSOCKET must be used to set up the listening socket before ACCEPT can be used.
all_commands.returns: The channel number to use to communicate with the client.

all_commands.description: This manual has detailed various functions to read and write to all of the ports. In communications code, a function or command

all_commands.name: PRINT
all_commands.description: This command sends data to the printer to be printed.

all_commands.name: OUTBYTE
all_commands.description: This command outputs a byte to a port.

all_commands.description: This is a non-blocking input function. It will read in all of the bytes available on the specified port.

all_commands.returns: Returns a 0 if there were no errors, otherwise a 1 is returned.
