all_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.length_remaining
all_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.length_remaining This command retrieves the length of ribbon remaining on the cartridge. This is specified in meters. If a cartridge is not installed, the printer returns "0". If the cartridge option is not available in the printer,

all_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.length
all_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.length This command returns the original length of the ribbon cartridge installed in the printer. This is specified in meters. If a ribbon cartridge is not installed, then the printer returns "0". If the ribbon cartridge option is not

all_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.authenticated
all_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.authenticated This command returns the printer cartridge authentication status. The setting gets updated every time an authentication occurs (power up, head close, or any other time).

all_commands.name: ribbon.cartridge.inserted
all_commands.description: ribbon.cartridge.inserted This command returns if the ribbon cartridge is inserted or not. The command is hidden in an ALLCV.

all_commands.name: ribbon.coating
all_commands.description: ribbon.coating This command sets the type of ribbon coating used.
possible_values: To configure the printer for the printer ribbon:

all_commands.name: ribbon.tension
all_commands.description: ribbon.tension This command sets the tension of the ribbon.

all_commands.name: rtc.exists
all_commands.description: rtc.exists This command reports whether the system has a real-time clock.
possible_values: "no" the system does not have a real-time clock.
"yes" the system has a real-time clock.

all_commands.name: rtc.date
all_commands.description: rtc.date The command sets the system date. The command accepts the month-day-year format, for example, "11-02-2021". If the format is not correct or the date is not valid, the command is ignored. The printer needs

all_commands.name: rtc.time
all_commands.description: rtc.time This command sets the system time. The time value must be in the hour:minute:second format, for example, 11:32:11. If the format is not correct or the time is not valid, the command is ignored. The printer

all_commands.name: rtc.timezone
all_commands.description: rtc.timezone This command specifies the POSIX-compliant time zone string. This string includes the following:
possible_values: www.iana.org/time-zones This site is updated periodically to reflect changes made by political
bodies to time zone boundaries, UTC offsets, and daylight-saving rules.

all_commands.name: rtc.unix_timestamp
all_commands.description: rtc.unix_timestamp This command sets or gets the printer time based on the Unix Epoch (UTC) number of seconds since January 1, 1970.

all_commands.name: sensor.air_pressure.current_reading
all_commands.description: sensor.air_pressure.current_reading This command returns the atmospheric pressure in millibars.
possible_values: "" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

all_commands.name: sensor.ambient_light.current_reading
all_commands.description: sensor.ambient_light.current_reading This command returns the ambient light value. The ambient light reading is reported in lux.
possible_values: "" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

all_commands.name: sensor.battery.in_volts
all_commands.description: sensor.battery.in_volts This command retrieves information on the battery current in volts.

all_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.brightness
all_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.brightness This command retrieves the current back bar sensor brightness level.

all_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.ppr_out_thold
all_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.ppr_out_thold This command retrieves the current back bar sensor paper out threshold value.

all_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.cur
all_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.cur This command retrieves the current back bar sensor value.

all_commands.name: sensor.cover_open
all_commands.description: sensor.cover_open This printer setting determines if the printer media cover is open.
possible_values: "yes" means the printer cover is open
"no" means the printer cover is closed

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.ppr_out_thold
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.ppr_out_thold This command retrieves the current paper out threshold level of the front bar sensor of the printer.

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.cur
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.cur This command retrieves the current front bar sensor value.

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.thold
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.thold This command retrieves the current front bar sensor threshold value.

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.gain
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.gain This command retrieves the current front bar sensor gain level.

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.brightness
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.brightness This command retrieves the current front bar sensor brightness.

all_commands.name: sensor.front_bar.offset
all_commands.description: sensor.front_bar.offset This command retrieves the current front bar sensor offset value.

all_commands.name: sensor.back_bar.offset
all_commands.description: sensor.back_bar.offset This command retrieves the current back bar sensor offset value.

all_commands.name: sensor.gap.thold
all_commands.description: sensor.gap.thold This command retrieves the current gap sensor threshold level.

all_commands.name: sensor.gap.offset
all_commands.description: sensor.gap.offset This command retrieves the current gap sensor offset value.

all_commands.name: sensor.gap.gain
all_commands.description: sensor.gap.gain This command retrieves the current gap sensor gain level.

all_commands.name: sensor.gap.brightness
all_commands.description: sensor.gap.brightness This command retrieves the current gap sensor brightness level.

all_commands.name: sensor.head.temp_avg
all_commands.description: sensor.head.temp_avg This command retrieves the current average head temperature in Celsius.

all_commands.name: sensor.head.temp_celsius
all_commands.description: sensor.head.temp_celsius This command retrieves the current head temperature in Celsius.

all_commands.name: sensor.head.temp
all_commands.description: sensor.head.temp This command retrieves the current head temperature of the printer.

all_commands.name: sensor.magnetometer.current_reading
all_commands.description: sensor.magnetometer.current_reading This command returns a magnetic induction reading in gauss.
possible_values: The magnetic induction in gauss. If the sensor is not installed, the getvar returns "".

all_commands.name: sensor.object_temperature.current_reading
all_commands.description: sensor.object_temperature.current_reading This command returns the temperature, in Celsius, from the sensor.
possible_values: Object temperature, in degrees Celsius, from "-20.0" to "200.0".
"" indicates that the temperature sensor is not installed.

all_commands.name: sensor.peel.thold
all_commands.description: sensor.peel.thold This command retrieves the current peel sensor threshold level.

all_commands.name: sensor.peel.gain
all_commands.description: sensor.peel.gain This command retrieves the current peel sensor gain level.

all_commands.name: sensor.paper_supply
all_commands.description: sensor.paper_supply Returns current paper supply status.

all_commands.name: sensor.peeler
all_commands.description: sensor.peeler Obtains current peeler sensor status.

all_commands.name: sensor.peel.brightness
all_commands.description: sensor.peel.brightness This command returns the current peel sensor brightness level.

all_commands.name: sensor.proximity.current_reading
all_commands.description: sensor.proximity.current_reading This command returns proximity information. The higher the number, the closer the item is.
possible_values: "0" to "4095" A higher number indicates closer proximity.
"" indicates that the sensor is not installed.

all_commands.name: sensor.width.in_dots
all_commands.description: sensor.width.in_dots This command retrieves the current width sensor value in dots.

all_commands.name: sensor.width.cur
all_commands.description: sensor.width.cur This command retrieves the current width sensor value.

all_commands.name: sensor.self_adjusting_enable
all_commands.description: sensor.self_adjusting_enable Enables the self-adjusting gap sensor.
possible_values: "yes" enables the self-adjusting gap sensor and disables the traditional gap sensor
"no" disables the self-adjusting gap sensor and enables the traditional gap sensor

all_commands.name: usb.device.device_id_string
all_commands.description: usb.device.device_id_string This command retrieves the manufacturer assigned IEEE1284 Device Identification string for USB devices.

all_commands.name: usb.device.device_unique_id
all_commands.description: usb.device.device_unique_id This command sets the USB Unique Device ID setting. The identifier that makes any printer unique is set by the "usb.device.serial_string" command which is reported to the USB driver.

all_commands.name: usb.device.device_version
all_commands.description: usb.device.device_version This command returns the version of the USB device being queried.

all_commands.name: usb.device.manufacturer_string
all_commands.description: usb.device.manufacturer_string This command retrieves the USB device manufacturer’s name.

all_commands.name: usb.device.product_id
all_commands.description: usb.device.product_id This command retrieves the Product Identification number that a manufacturer assigned to a particular product. This number, along with the Vendor ID, allows a USB host to distinguish between devices.

all_commands.name: usb.device.product_string
all_commands.description: usb.device.product_string This command returns the manufacturer-assigned string describing a particular USB product.

all_commands.name: usb.device.serial_string
all_commands.description: usb.device.serial_string This command returns the manufacturer-assigned serial number for a particular USB product.

all_commands.name: usb.device.vendor_id
all_commands.description: usb.device.vendor_id This command returns the Vendor Identification number that the USB-IF organization has assigned to a manufacturer. This number, along with the Product ID, allows a USB host to distinguish between devices.

all_commands.name: usb.halt
all_commands.description: usb.halt This command controls whether the printer allows communication over the USB port when the printer is in an error condition.

all_commands.name: usb.host.config_info_to_usb
all_commands.description: usb.host.config_info_to_usb This command is used by WML to save the ^HH output files to the USB thumb drive. The file names are written in the CONFIGxxx.TXT format, where xxx ranges from 1 to 999.

all_commands.name: usb.host.fn_field_data
all_commands.description: usb.host.fn_field_data This command is used to collect a user’s response to a presented ^FN prompt. IMPORTANT: This command is used only in the context of the on-printer Print Station application.
possible_values: The text entered by the user via a USB Human Interface Device (HID) keyboard.

all_commands.name: usb.host.fn_last_field
all_commands.description: usb.host.fn_last_field This command is intended for use by WML code to control the presentation of ^FN fields contained within a template file that resides on the E:/ drive and has an extension of .ZPL.

all_commands.name: usb.host.hid_count
all_commands.description: usb.host.hid_count This command displays the number of USB Human Interface Devices (HIDs) connected to the printer. Refer to http://www.usb.org for further details on USB device types.

all_commands.name: usb.host.keyboard_input
all_commands.description: usb.host.keyboard_input This command enables/disables USB keyboard input to the printer, affecting the Print Station user menu item.
possible_values: "off" means keyboard input is not supported

all_commands.name: usb.host.lock_out
all_commands.description: usb.host.lock_out This command enables/disables the USB host port.

all_commands.name: usb.host.mass_storage_count
all_commands.description: usb.host.mass_storage_count This command displays the number of USB mass storage devices connected to the printer. Only the first USB mass storage device found will be mounted and accessible.

all_commands.name: usb.host.read_list
all_commands.description: usb.host.read_list This command scans the mounted usb mass storage device for non-user-restricted files and displays the files in a list.
possible_values: "fill_store" The printer creates a list of all of the top-level files that are readable on a
connected mass storage device. (.ZPL and .XML files)
"store" The printer copies the current file (the file listed on the display) or all eligible files if
SELECT ALL is displayed from the USB mass storage device to the printer’s E: drive.
NOTE: "store" does an exact byte-for-byte copy of the file being stored. ZPL files
that are transferred to the printer using the “store” command are NOT prepared to
be used with a recall format command (^XF). See XREF Character Substitution (in
Mirror) for the modifications necessary to prepare a ZPL file for use with ^XF. If the
ZPL file contains a ^DF, the appropriate way to place it on the printer’s memory is to

all_commands.name: usb.host.read_list_print_delay
all_commands.description: usb.host.read_list_print_delay This command specifies a number of milliseconds for the printer to wait before processing the next file when “SELECT ALL” is chosen on the USB PRINT FILES user menu.

all_commands.name: usb.host.template_list
all_commands.description: usb.host.template_list This command is used by WML to support selecting .ZPL template files resident on the E:/ drive.
possible_values: "fill" The printer analyzes the contents of its E:/ drive and creates a list of the template files
"up" moves to the previous file in the list
"down" moves to the next file in the list

all_commands.name: usb.host.template_print_amount
all_commands.description: usb.host.template_print_amount This command is used by WML to control the number of template-type labels to print.
possible_values: "up" moves to the previous file in the list
"down" moves to the next file in the list
all_commands.default: "1" which will change based on the contents of the selected template file

all_commands.name: usb.host.write_list
all_commands.description: usb.host.write_list This command scans the E: flash drive for non-user-restricted files and displays the files in a list.
possible_values: "fill_store" The printer analyzes the contents of its E: drive and creates a list of files that
may be copied to a USB mass storage device connected to the printer.
"store" The printer copies the current file (the file listed on the display) or all eligible files if
"SELECT ALL" is displayed to the USB mass storage device.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.appl_path
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.appl_path This command specifies the path to the location on a USB device from which Mirror files are retrieved. If no path is specified, then the path is zebra/appl.
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.auto
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.auto This command determines if mirroring happens automatically when a USB device is inserted in the printer. To use this function, the setting for usb.mirror.enable must be "on".
possible_values: "on" Mirroring occurs automatically when the USB device is inserted and
"off" Mirroring does not occur automatically when the USB device is inserted.
"prompt" The printer gives you the option to start or abort a mirroring process.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.enable
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.enable This command enables or disables the ability to perform mirroring of a USB device.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.enabled
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.enabled Enables or disables the ability to perform mirroring using a USB device memory stick.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.error_retry
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.error_retry This command specifies the number of times that the USB mirror operation will be repeated if the process fails.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.auto
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.auto This command determines if a feedback file is written to the USB device connected to the printer after mirroring.
possible_values: "on" A feedback file is written to the USB device connected to the printer.
"off" A feeback file is not written to the USB device connected to the printer.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.odometer
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.odometer This command instructs the printer to set or retrieve the usb.mirror.feedback.odometer value.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.feedback.path
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.feedback.path This command specifies where the feedback file is stored on the USB drive connected to the printer.
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters
NOTE: The path must exist on the USB drive before the printer can write files to it.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.fetch
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.fetch This command immediately initiates a USB mirroring operation. To use this function, the setting for usb.mirror.enable must be "on".

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.last_error
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.last_error This command returns the last USB mirroring error string. If there are no errors, the result is "No Error".

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.last_time
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.last_time This command returns the date and time of the last USB mirroring operation. The date and time reported are from the printer’s clock.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.path
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.path This command specifies the root directory on the connected USB drive. The root directory contains the subdirectories from which files are retrieved during the mirror operation. If no path is specified, then the
possible_values: A valid path up to 255 characters.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.reset_delay
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.reset_delay This command specifies a number of seconds for the printer to wait after it loads the last of the files in the /commands directory during mirroring.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.success
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.success This command returns the last USB mirroring event status string.
possible_values: "yes" Indicates that the mirroring operation was successful.
"no" Indicates that the mirroring operation was not successful.

all_commands.name: usb.mirror.success_time
all_commands.description: usb.mirror.success_time This command returns the date and time of the last successful USB mirroring operation. The date and time reported are from the printer’s clock.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.add_breakpoint
all_commands.description: zbi.control.add_breakpoint This command instructs the printer to set a ZBI program break point.
possible_values: Any line number of the program currently being debugged.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.break
all_commands.description: zbi.control.break This command breaks the execution of the ZBI 2.0 program that is currently running.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.clear_breakpoints
all_commands.description: zbi.control.clear_breakpoints This command deletes all breakpoints in the current ZBI 2.0 program.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.delete_breakpoint
all_commands.description: zbi.control.delete_breakpoint This command deletes a breakpoint in the current ZBI 2.0 program.
possible_values: You can use the same value as add_breakpoint.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.line_number
all_commands.description: zbi.control.line_number This command gives you control and information about which line of a stopped ZBI 2.0 program is being executed.
possible_values: Any line number of the currently stopped ZBI program.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.restart
all_commands.description: zbi.control.restart This command restarts a ZBI 2.0 program that is currently stopped.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.run
all_commands.description: zbi.control.run This command runs the current ZBI 2.0 program that is loaded in the interpreter.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.step
all_commands.description: zbi.control.step This command restarts the execution of the currently stopped ZBI 2.0 program for one line.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.terminate
all_commands.description: zbi.control.terminate This command instructs the ZBI 2.0 program to terminate and shuts down the interpreter.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.variable_name
all_commands.description: zbi.control.variable_name This command sets the name of the variable that is to be read or modified through variable_value.
possible_values: Any ZBI variable in the program that is currently being debugged.

all_commands.name: zbi.control.variable_value
all_commands.description: zbi.control.variable_value This command identifies the variable name.
possible_values: A string or integer that is dependent on the variable type in variable_name.
all_commands.default: The current value of the variable referenced by variable_name.

all_commands.name: zbi.enable
all_commands.description: zbi.enable This command enables ZBI on the printer.

all_commands.name: zbi.key
all_commands.description: zbi.key This command identifies if the ZBI 2.0 option is enabled or disabled on the printer.

all_commands.name: zbi.last_error
all_commands.description: zbi.last_error This command identifies the last error that the ZBI 2.0 interpreter encountered.

all_commands.name: zbi.program_list
all_commands.description: zbi.program_list This SGD is intended to be used on WML pages. It purpose is to support displaying the name of each ZBI program file contained on the E: drive.
possible_values: "up" gets the previous file in the list
"down" gets the next file in the list
"execute" executes the currently specified zbi file (as determined by the getvar command)

all_commands.name: zbi.reseller_key
all_commands.description: zbi.reseller_key This command allows programs that are encrypted with this key in ZBI- Developer to run.
possible_values: Any valid encryption key provided by ZBI Developer.

all_commands.name: zbi.revision
all_commands.description: zbi.revision This command identifies the current ZBI version.

all_commands.name: zbi.running_program_name
all_commands.description: zbi.running_program_name This command identifies the name of the ZBI 2.0 program that is currently running.

all_commands.name: zbi.start_info.execute
all_commands.description: zbi.start_info.execute This command instructs the ZBI 2.0 environment to execute the program listed in the file_name.

all_commands.name: zbi.start_info.file_name
all_commands.description: zbi.start_info.file_name This command prepares a program to run when the zbi.start_info.execute command is used. This command does not run the program.
possible_values: A file name or path of a basic program
all_commands.default: The last program run. If nothing has been run, "*:\.BAZ".

all_commands.name: zbi.start_info.memory_alloc
all_commands.description: zbi.start_info.memory_alloc This command identifies the amount of memory currently in use in a ZBI 2.0 program.

all_commands.name: zbi.state
all_commands.description: zbi.state This command shows the current state of the ZBI 2.0 program.
possible_values: "running" ZBI Interpreter is active and running a program
"stopped" ZBI Interpreter is active but not executing a program

all_commands.name: zpl.calibrate
all_commands.description: zpl.calibrate This command measures the media label length that is installed in the printer. It then sets the "zpl.label_length" parameter to the detected media label length.

all_commands.name: zpl.format_prefix
all_commands.description: zpl.format_prefix This command sets or returns the format character to the character corresponding to the ASCII Hex value xx. This command is similar to the ^CC and ~CC commands.
possible_values: Specifying the up or down will increment or decrement the current value.
Note that the increment/decrement will skip over conflicting values.
Conflicting values for zpl.format_prefix are zpl.command_prefix, and

all_commands.name: zpl.caret
all_commands.description: zpl.caret This command is used to change the format command prefix for ZPL commands. The default prefix is the caret (^)

all_commands.name: zpl.control_character
all_commands.description: zpl.control_character This command is used to change the control command prefix. The default prefix is the tilde (~). This command is equivalent to the ^CT and ~CT commands.
possible_values: ASCII values for the desired character "00-FF,00-ff,up,down"
See ASCII on page 1555 for more information.

all_commands.name: zpl.delimiter
all_commands.description: zpl.delimiter This command is used to change the delimiter character for ZPL commands. The default delimiter character is the comma (,).
possible_values: HEX values for the desired character "00-FF,00-ff,up,down"
See ASCII on page 1555 for more information.

all_commands.name: zpl.label_length
all_commands.description: zpl.label_length This command defines the length of the label. This command is necessary when using continuous media (media that is not divided into separate labels by gaps, spaces, notches, slots, or holes).
possible_values: "1" to "32000", (in dots) not to exceed the maximum label length.
While the printer accepts any value for this parameter, the amount of memory installed determines
the maximum length of the label.

all_commands.name: zpl.label_length_always
all_commands.description: zpl.label_length_always This command allows the label length defined by ^LL to apply when the media is Gap or Black Mark. This command is persistent across a power cycle.
possible_values: "yes" applies the label length to all media.
"no" causes the label length to apply only to continuous media.

all_commands.name: zpl.label_orientation
all_commands.description: zpl.label_orientation This command instructs the printer to rotate the entire label output by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees.

all_commands.name: zpl.left_position
all_commands.description: zpl.left_position This command sets the label’s left margin offset in dots. Related Command: ^LS

all_commands.name: zpl.system_error
all_commands.description: zpl.system_error This command returns the system error flags. This command is equivalent to the error recording of ~HQES.

all_commands.name: zpl.system_status
all_commands.description: zpl.system_status This command returns the errors and warnings of the system. This command is equivalent to all data reported by the ~HQES ZPL command.

all_commands.name: zpl.zpl_mode
all_commands.description: zpl.zpl_mode This command sets the ZPL mode to ZPL II or ZPL.

all_commands.name: zpl.zpl_override
all_commands.description: zpl.zpl_override Enable this menu item to prevent the following ZPL commands from changing the printer’s current settings: • ^MM (print mode)
possible_values: "enabled" prevents ZPL commands from overriding printer settings.

all_commands.name: zpl.relative_darkness
all_commands.description: zpl.relative_darkness Changes the relative darkness for ZPL labels. This command is similar to the ZPL ^MD command. IMPORTANT: This value is saved permanently on Desktop printers, but it is not saved

all_commands.name: bluetooth.address
all_commands.description: bluetooth.address This command returns the printer’s Bluetooth device address.

all_commands.name: bluetooth.afh_map
all_commands.description: bluetooth.afh_map Sets or retrieves the default AFH (adaptive frequency hopping) channel map (Bluetooth radios 1.2 and later); 20 bytes.

all_commands.name: bluetooth.afh_map_curr
all_commands.description: bluetooth.afh_map_curr This command retrieves the current AFH (adaptive frequency hopping) channel map (Bluetooth radios 1.2 and later).

all_commands.name: bluetooth.afh_mode
all_commands.description: bluetooth.afh_mode This command sets or retrieves AFH (adaptive frequency hopping) mode setting (Bluetooth radios 1.2 and later).

all_commands.name: bluetooth.allow_non_display_numeric_comparison
all_commands.description: bluetooth.allow_non_display_numeric_comparison This command allows the user to enable or disable a numeric comparison connection for printers without a display and also enables or disables displaying the pass key.
possible_values: "off" Does not allow pass key connection for non display printers.
"print" Prints and accepts the pass key on non display printers (Man in the Middle
"no print" Accepts but does not print the pass key for non display printer (no Man in the

all_commands.name: bluetooth.authentication
all_commands.description: bluetooth.authentication This command sets or retrieves Bluetooth authentication mode and works in combination with the bluetooth.bluetooth_pin.
possible_values: "off" disables authentication (can connect to master device without PIN)
"setpin" enables authentication (requires PIN or passkey to connect to a master device)

all_commands.name: bluetooth.bluetooth_pin
all_commands.description: bluetooth.bluetooth_pin This command is used to connect to the printer only when the command bluetooth.authentication is set to "setpin".
possible_values: Any text string up to 10 characters

all_commands.name: bluetooth.clear_bonding_cache
all_commands.description: bluetooth.clear_bonding_cache Deletes all information related to previous Bluetooth pairing events from the printer. Do

all_commands.name: bluetooth.date
all_commands.description: bluetooth.date This command shows the release date of the Bluetooth module.

all_commands.name: bluetooth.discoverable
all_commands.description: bluetooth.discoverable This command enables or disables the Bluetooth discoverable mode.
all_commands.default: "on" for Printers running Link-OS v5.3 or earlier versions

all_commands.name: bluetooth.enable
all_commands.description: bluetooth.enable This command enables or disables the Bluetooth radio.

all_commands.name: bluetooth.enable_reconnect
all_commands.description: bluetooth.enable_reconnect Enables the Bluetooth reconnect feature required by iOS devices.

all_commands.name: ip.dhcp.enable

"on" printer uses DHCP to get the IP address

"off" turns off the auto mirroring feature

all_commands.name: ip.mirror.error_retry

all_commands.description: ip.mirror.username This command specifies the user name on the mirroring server assigned for mirroring updates (fetch).

all_commands.name: ip.mirror.version

all_commands.name: ip.netmask
